narrative:
The model determined that you have a 58% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the loan amount you requested, the status of your checking account, and the level of savings you have. The large size of the loan you applied for was the single biggest reason for the rejection. At 13,756 DM, your request was more than four times higher than the average amount approved applicants ask for. This high amount pushed the prediction strongly toward bad credit risk.

Your checking account status of having no account worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward approval. Similarly, having unknown or no savings also pushed the decision in a positive direction compared with many approved applicants. However, these two helpful factors were not enough to overcome the negative impact of the very large loan size.

You should consider reapplying for a substantially smaller loan amount that is closer to what the bank typically approves. Paying closer attention to maintaining a visible checking account balance and building some savings before you apply again may also improve your chances.
